title: Beatrix and the Deadline
premise: Jonah Yarrow, a former analyst for the private intelligence firm Halcyon Verity, has spent three years buried under four identities after exposing the firm's market-manipulation program. When a woman named Beatrix Kade appears claiming he once saved her life—a favor he has no memory of—she demands repayment: help her destroy Halcyon's Frankfurt trading node before Thursday's market open, or she exposes his current alias to the people hunting him. As they race across Europe dismantling the network that trained them both, Jonah discovers Beatrix is the daughter of the analyst whose death triggered his whistle-blowing, and that his 'forgotten' favor was a lie engineered to recruit him. In the end, Jonah chooses truth over survival, broadcasting Halcyon's ledger live as Frankfurt opens, and Beatrix must decide whether loyalty to her father's memory or to the man who helped her matters more.
about_author: Emrys Marchetti is the pen name of a former financial journalist who spent a decade covering market irregularities before turning to fiction. They write from a small flat in Lisbon, where they claim the best plot ideas arrive during power outages.

chapters.title: Four Names, No Sleep
chapters.summary: Jonah Yarrow, living quietly in Rotterdam as 'Daniel Voss', wakes at 3 a.m. to his usual insomnia and rehearses his cover routines. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: brittle vigilance—the exhausting cost of a life built on erasure.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: A woman leaves an envelope at Jonah's workplace containing photos of himself under a name he abandoned two years ago, plus a note: 'You saved my life in Vienna. Interest is owed.' POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: cold dread—the past has found a crack in the wall.

chapters.title: Beatrix
chapters.summary: Jonah confronts the stranger, Beatrix Kade, who is calm, prepared, and knows his sleep patterns better than he does. She gives him 96 hours. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: cornered fascination—he can't tell if she's a threat or a mirror.

chapters.title: What Halcyon Trained Us For
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: Jonah's recruitment into Halcyon Verity's analyst program, the tradecraft, the quiet moral erosion. POV: Jonah (past). Emotional beat: seduction and complicity—how good men learn to look away.

chapters.title: The Ledger Under the Floor
chapters.summary: Beatrix reveals her target: Halcyon's Frankfurt node executes manipulative trades every morning; a cached ledger there could burn the whole network. She needs someone who knows the building. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: controlled fury disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: Vienna, Three Years Ago
chapters.summary: Beatrix recounts the night in Vienna when, she says, Jonah pulled her from a staged car crash meant to silence her father's investigation. Jonah remembers no such night—and says so. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into purpose.

chapters.title: The Handler's Call
chapters.summary: Jonah's old handler, Marek, contacts him through a dead-drop protocol: Halcyon knows Beatrix found him, and offers him a way back in—if he delivers her. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: terror sharpened into temptation—safety offered at an unbearable price.

chapters.title: Train to Cologne
chapters.summary: Jonah pretends to accept Marek's deal while traveling with Beatrix to meet her inside contact at the node. The two trade truths on a night train, neither fully trusting. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: wary intimacy—two liars recognizing each other's craft.

chapters.title: The Contact Who Was Already Dead
chapters.summary: Their Cologne contact is found drowned hours before the meeting; it's framed as suicide but the staging is Halcyon-perfect. Someone inside is feeding Marek their route. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: paranoia closing like a fist.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Beatrix admits parts of her story don't add up under Jonah's questioning; the Vienna rescue happened—but not the way she told it. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: shame cracking open—her mission may be built on a curated lie.

chapters.title: Marek's Offer, Written Down
chapters.summary: Marek meets Jonah alone in a Cologne hotel bar, laying out full reinstatement, new identity, protection—in exchange for Beatrix. He also reveals Beatrix's real surname. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: vertigo—the deal is everything he's been starving for.

chapters.title: The Analyst's Daughter
chapters.summary: Beatrix is the daughter of Elias Kade, the Halcyon analyst whose suspicious death preceded Jonah's whistle-blowing. Her revenge and his guilt are the same event viewed from opposite ends. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: guilt made flesh—the person his conscience has been wearing all along.

chapters.title: Frankfurt, Wednesday Night
chapters.summary: They infiltrate the node's periphery using Jonah's old access patterns, discovering security upgraded specifically against him—someone predicted this exact move. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: hunted clarity—he was never invisible, only stored.

chapters.title: The Mole in the Plan
chapters.summary: Beatrix discovers her own recruiter fed her the Frankfurt plan knowing it would flush Jonah out; she was bait from the start. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: betrayal upon betrayal—rage redirected inward.

chapters.title: Sleep, Finally
chapters.summary: On the eve of the deadline, exhausted and exposed, Jonah sleeps four hours for the first time in years—because Beatrix keeps watch. A quiet chapter of confession and near-tenderness. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: love arriving precisely when survival is least likely.

chapters.title: Thursday, 08:59
chapters.summary: They breach the node minutes before market open; Jonah begins extracting the ledger while Beatrix holds the door against Halcyon's response team. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: adrenaline and resolve—no exit plan, only forward.

chapters.title: Burn the Network
chapters.summary: Jonay faces the choice: broadcast the ledger (destroying himself with it) or take Marek's escape. He uploads everything live as Frankfurt opens, markets convulsing in real time. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: liberation through self-immolation—truth as the last identity left.

chapters.title: The Man in the Server Room
chapters.summary: Marek arrives personally; a brutal, close-quarters confrontation ends with Marek dead by Beatrix's hand—her first kill, done to save Jonah. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: horror and fierce protectiveness entangled.

chapters.title: Aftermath of the Open
chapters.summary: Halcyon Verity collapses publicly; regulators swarm; both protagonists are now the most identifiable fugitives in Europe. They hide in a safehouse as news cycles detonate. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: hollow triumph—they won, and winning cost everything.

chapters.title: What Elias Would Have Wanted
chapters.summary: Beatrix reads her father's recovered files and learns he had planned to blow the whistle himself; her revenge completes his unfinished act. She releases her claim on vengeance. POV: Beatrix. Emotional beat: mourning resolved into inheritance.

chapters.title: A Fifth Name
chapters.summary: Jonah offers Beatrix the one thing he has expertise in: how to disappear well—together, this time, rather than apart. They build new identities side by side. POV: Jonah. Emotional beat: cautious hope—survival shared becomes a life.

chapters.title: Beatrix and the Deadline
chapters.summary: One year later: a quiet coastal town, a market report about Halcyon's former executives facing trial, and Jonah sleeping through the night beside Beatrix. A final envelope arrives—unopened, they burn it unread. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: peace earned, guarded, and finally real.
